sanskrit: tasmin raudre tathā yuddhe vartamāne mahābhaye prāvartata nadī ghorā śoṇitāntrataraṅgiṇī
english: While that savage and terrifying battle raged on, there arose a ghastly river whose waves were blood and entrails.

sanskrit: asthisaṃcayasaṃghāṭā keśaśaivalaśādvalā rathahradā śarāvartā hayamīnā durāsadā
english: Heaps of bones were its rafts, hair its moss and grass; chariots were its pools, arrows its whirlpools, horses its fish—an unfordable stream.

sanskrit: śīrṣopalasamākīrṇā hastigrāhasamākulā kavacoṣṇīṣaphenāḍhyā dhanurdvīpāsikacchapā
english: Strewn with severed heads for stones, teeming with elephants for crocodiles, foaming with armor and turbans, with bows for islands and swords for turtles.

sanskrit: patākādhvajavṛkṣāḍhyā martyakūlāpahāriṇī kravyādasaṃghasaṃkīrṇā yamarāṣṭravivardhinī
english: Rich with banners and standards for trees, sweeping away the banks of men, thronged with packs of carrion-eaters, swelling the realm of Yama.

sanskrit: tāṃ nadīṃ kṣatriyāḥ śūrā hayanāgarathaplavaiḥ praterur bahavo rājan bhayaṃ tyaktvā mahāhave
english: That river, O king, the brave warriors crossed in their multitudes by rafts of horses, elephants, and chariots, casting off fear in the great battle.

sanskrit: apovāha raṇe bhīrūn kaśmalenābhisaṃvṛtān yathā vaitaraṇī pretān pretarājapuraṃ prati
english: It bore away the cowards in the fray, overcome with stupefaction, as the Vaitaraṇī bears the dead toward the city of the king of the dead.

sanskrit: prākrośan kṣatriyās tatra dṛṣṭvā tad vaiśasaṃ mahat duryodhanāparādhena kṣayaṃ gacchanti kauravāḥ
english: Beholding that great slaughter, the warriors there cried aloud: "Through Duryodhana's offense the Kauravas are going to ruin!"

sanskrit: guṇavatsu kathaṃ dveṣaṃ dhārtarāṣṭro janeśvaraḥ kṛtavān pāṇḍuputreṣu pāpātmā lobhamohitaḥ
english: "How could that lord of men, the son of Dhṛtarāṣṭra, evil of soul and deluded by greed, conceive such hatred for the virtuous sons of Pāṇḍu?"

sanskrit: evaṃ bahuvidhā vācaḥ śrūyante smātra bhārata pāṇḍavastavasaṃyuktāḥ putrāṇāṃ te sudāruṇāḥ
english: Words of many kinds such as these were heard there, O Bhārata—praising the Pāṇḍavas and most harsh toward your sons.

sanskrit: tā niśamya tadā vācaḥ sarvayodhair udāhṛtāḥ āgaskṛt sarvalokasya putro duryodhanas tava
english: Hearing those words then uttered by all the warriors, your son Duryodhana—the offender against the whole world—

sanskrit: bhīṣmaṃ droṇaṃ kṛpaṃ caiva śalyaṃ covāca bhārata yudhyadhvam anahaṃkārāḥ kiṃ ciraṃ kurutheti ca
english: spoke to Bhīṣma, Droṇa, Kṛpa, and Śalya, O Bhārata: "Fight without arrogance! Why do you delay so long?"

sanskrit: tataḥ pravavṛte yuddhaṃ kurūṇāṃ pāṇḍavaiḥ saha akṣadyūtakṛtaṃ rājan sughoraṃ vaiśasaṃ tadā
english: Then, O king, there broke out between the Kurus and the Pāṇḍavas that most dreadful carnage, born of the game of dice.

sanskrit: yat purā na nigṛhṇīṣe vāryamāṇo mahātmabhiḥ vaicitravīrya tasyedaṃ phalaṃ paśya tathāvidham
english: That which you would not restrain of old, though warned by the great-souled ones—O son of Vicitravīrya, behold now its fruit, just such as this.

sanskrit: na hi pāṇḍusutā rājan sasainyāḥ sapadānugāḥ rakṣanti samare prāṇān kauravā vā viśāṃ pate
english: For neither the sons of Pāṇḍu with their armies and followers, nor the Kauravas, O lord of peoples, spared their own lives in that battle.

sanskrit: etasmāt kāraṇād ghoro vartate sma janakṣayaḥ daivād vā puruṣavyāghra tava cāpanayān nṛpa
english: From this cause, O tiger among men, that terrible destruction of men came to pass—whether by fate, O king, or by your own misrule.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca arjunas tu naravyāghra suśarmapramukhān nṛpān anayat pretarājasya bhavanaṃ sāyakaiḥ śitaiḥ
english: Saṃjaya said: But Arjuna, O tiger among men, with his sharpened arrows led the kings headed by Suśarman to the abode of the king of the dead.

sanskrit: suśarmāpi tato bāṇaiḥ pārthaṃ vivyādha saṃyuge vāsudevaṃ ca saptatyā pārthaṃ ca navabhiḥ punaḥ
english: Suśarman too then pierced Pārtha with arrows in the fray, striking Vāsudeva with seventy and Pārtha again with nine.

sanskrit: tān nivārya śaraugheṇa śakrasūnur mahārathaḥ suśarmaṇo raṇe yodhān prāhiṇod yamasādanam
english: Warding them off with a flood of arrows, the son of Śakra, that mighty car-warrior, sent Suśarman's fighters in battle to the dwelling of Yama.

sanskrit: te vadhyamānāḥ pārthena kāleneva yugakṣaye vyadravanta raṇe rājan bhaye jāte mahārathāḥ
english: Slaughtered by Pārtha as if by Time at the dissolution of the age, those mighty car-warriors fled the battle, O king, when terror seized them.

sanskrit: utsṛjya turagān ke cid rathān ke cic ca māriṣa gajān anye samutsṛjya prādravanta diśo daśa
english: Some abandoning their horses, some their chariots, O venerable one, and others forsaking their elephants, fled in all ten directions.

sanskrit: apare tudyamānās tu vājināgarathā raṇāt tvarayā parayā yuktāḥ prādravanta viśāṃ pate
english: Others, goading on their horses, elephants, and chariots, fled from the battle with the utmost haste, O lord of peoples.

sanskrit: pādātāś cāpi śastrāṇi samutsṛjya mahāraṇe nirapekṣā vyadhāvanta tena tena sma bhārata
english: And the foot-soldiers too, casting away their weapons in that great battle, ran heedlessly this way and that, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: vāryamāṇāḥ sma bahuśas traigartena suśarmaṇā tathānyaiḥ pārthivaśreṣṭhair na vyatiṣṭhanta saṃyuge
english: Though restrained again and again by the Trigarta Suśarman and by the other foremost kings, they would not stand firm in the conflict.

sanskrit: tad balaṃ pradrutaṃ dṛṣṭvā putro duryodhanas tava puraskṛtya raṇe bhīṣmaṃ sarvasainyapuraskṛtam
english: Seeing that force in flight, your son Duryodhana, setting Bhīṣma before him in battle—Bhīṣma whom all the host placed at its head—

sanskrit: sarvodyogena mahatā dhanaṃjayam upādravat trigartādhipater arthe jīvitasya viśāṃ pate
english: with a great and total effort rushed upon Dhanaṃjaya, for the sake of the Trigarta lord's life, O lord of peoples.

sanskrit: sa ekaḥ samare tasthau kiran bahuvidhāñ śarān bhrātṛbhiḥ sahitaḥ sarvaiḥ śeṣā vipradrutā narāḥ
english: He alone stood firm in the fight, scattering arrows of many kinds, together with all his brothers, while the rest of the men had fled away.

sanskrit: tathaiva paṇḍavā rājan sarvodyogena daṃśitāḥ prayayuḥ phalgunārthāya yatra bhīṣmo vyavasthitaḥ
english: Likewise the Pāṇḍavas, O king, mail-clad with their whole strength, advanced for Phalguna's sake to where Bhīṣma had taken his stand.

sanskrit: jānanto 'pi raṇe śauryaṃ ghoraṃ gāṇḍīvadhanvanaḥ hāhākārakṛtotsāhā bhīṣmaṃ jagmuḥ samantataḥ
english: Though they knew the terrible valor in battle of the wielder of Gāṇḍīva, their ardor roused by cries of dismay, they assailed Bhīṣma on every side.

sanskrit: tatas tāladhvajaḥ śūraḥ pāṇḍavānām anīkinīm chādayām āsa samare śaraiḥ saṃnataparvabhiḥ
english: Then the hero of the palm-tree banner covered the host of the Pāṇḍavas in battle with arrows whose joints were smoothly bent.

sanskrit: ekībhūtās tataḥ sarve kuravaḥ pāṇḍavaiḥ saha ayudhyanta mahārāja madhyaṃ prāpte divākare
english: Then, gathered into one, all the Kurus together with the Pāṇḍavas fought on, O great king, when the sun had reached its zenith.

sanskrit: sātyakiḥ kṛtavarmāṇaṃ viddhvā pañcabhir āyasaiḥ atiṣṭhad āhave śūraḥ kiran bāṇān sahasraśaḥ
english: Sātyaki, having pierced Kṛtavarman with five iron shafts, stood his ground in the fray, that hero scattering arrows by the thousand.

sanskrit: tathaiva drupado rājā droṇaṃ viddhvā śitaiḥ śaraiḥ punar vivyādha saptatyā sārathiṃ cāsya saptabhiḥ
english: Likewise King Drupada, piercing Droṇa with sharp arrows, struck him again with seventy and his charioteer with seven.

sanskrit: bhīmasenas tu rājānaṃ bāhlikaṃ prapitāmaham viddhvānadan mahānādaṃ śārdūla iva kānane
english: And Bhīmasena, having pierced King Bāhlika, his great-grandsire, roared a mighty roar like a tiger in the forest.

sanskrit: ārjuniś citrasenena viddho bahubhir āśugaiḥ citrasenaṃ tribhir bāṇair vivyādha hṛdaye bhṛśam
english: Arjuna's son, pierced by Citrasena with many swift shafts, struck Citrasena deep in the heart with three arrows.

sanskrit: samāgatau tau tu raṇe mahāmātrau vyarocatām yathā divi mahāghorau rājan budhaśanaiścarau
english: Those two great champions, met together in battle, shone forth like the two most dread planets in the sky, O king—Mercury and Saturn.

sanskrit: tasyāśvāṃś caturo hatvā sūtaṃ ca navabhiḥ śaraiḥ nanāda balavan nādaṃ saubhadraḥ paravīrahā
english: Having slain his four horses and his charioteer with nine arrows, the son of Subhadrā, slayer of enemy heroes, roared a mighty roar.

sanskrit: hatāśvāt tu rathāt tūrṇam avaplutya mahārathaḥ āruroha rathaṃ tūrṇaṃ durmukhasya viśāṃ pate
english: Then that mighty car-warrior, swiftly leaping down from his horseless chariot, swiftly mounted the car of Durmukha, O lord of peoples.

sanskrit: droṇaś ca drupadaṃ viddhvā śaraiḥ saṃnataparvabhiḥ sārathiṃ cāsya vivyādha tvaramāṇaḥ parākramī
english: And Droṇa, having pierced Drupada with arrows of smoothly bent joints, in his haste, that valiant one, struck his charioteer as well.

sanskrit: pīḍyamānas tato rājā drupado vāhinīmukhe apāyāj javanair aśvaiḥ pūrvavairam anusmaran
english: Hard pressed then at the head of the host, King Drupada withdrew with his swift horses, recalling their ancient enmity.

sanskrit: bhīmasenas tu rājānaṃ muhūrtād iva bāhlikam vyaśvasūtarathaṃ cakre sarvasainyasya paśyataḥ
english: But Bhīmasena, in but a moment, stripped King Bāhlika of horses, charioteer, and car, before the eyes of the whole army.

sanskrit: sasaṃbhramo mahārāja saṃśayaṃ paramaṃ gataḥ avaplutya tato vāhād bāhlikaḥ puruṣottamaḥ āruroha rathaṃ tūrṇaṃ lakṣmaṇasya mahārathaḥ
english: In confusion, O great king, fallen into the gravest peril, Bāhlika, that best of men, leaping down from his mount, swiftly mounted the chariot of Lakṣmaṇa, that mighty car-warrior.

sanskrit: sātyakiḥ kṛtavarmāṇaṃ vārayitvā mahārathaḥ śarair bahuvidhai rājann āsasāda pitāmaham
english: Sātyaki, that mighty car-warrior, having warded off Kṛtavarman with arrows of many kinds, O king, closed upon the grandsire.

sanskrit: sa viddhvā bhārataṃ ṣaṣṭyā niśitair lomavāhibhiḥ nanarteva rathopasthe vidhunvāno mahad dhanuḥ
english: Having pierced the Bhārata with sixty keen feathered shafts, he seemed to dance upon his chariot-platform, shaking his great bow.

sanskrit: tasyāyasīṃ mahāśaktiṃ cikṣepātha pitāmahaḥ hemacitrāṃ mahāvegāṃ nāgakanyopamāṃ śubhām
english: At him the grandsire then hurled a great iron lance, gold-adorned, of mighty speed, beautiful as a serpent-maiden.

sanskrit: tām āpatantīṃ sahasā mṛtyukalpāṃ sutejanām dhvaṃsayām āsa vārṣṇeyo lāghavena mahāyaśāḥ
english: As it suddenly flew at him, death-like and keenly bright, the Vārṣṇeya of great renown shattered it by his deftness.

sanskrit: anāsādya tu vārṣṇeyaṃ śaktiḥ paramadāruṇā nyapatad dharaṇīpṛṣṭhe maholkeva gataprabhā
english: Failing to reach the Vārṣṇeya, that most dreadful lance fell upon the surface of the earth like a great meteor whose light had failed.

sanskrit: vārṣṇeyas tu tato rājan svāṃ śaktiṃ ghoradarśanām vegavad gṛhya cikṣepa pitāmaharathaṃ prati
english: Then the Vārṣṇeya, O king, seizing his own lance of dreadful aspect, hurled it with speed toward the grandsire's chariot.

sanskrit: vārṣṇeyabhujavegena praṇunnā sā mahāhave abhidudrāva vegena kālarātrir yathā naram
english: Driven by the force of the Vārṣṇeya's arm, in that great battle it rushed swiftly on like the Night of Doom upon a man.

sanskrit: tām āpatantīṃ sahasā dvidhā ciccheda bhārata kṣuraprābhyāṃ sutīkṣṇābhyāṃ sānvakīryata bhūtale
english: As it suddenly flew at him, he cut it in two, O Bhārata, with two razor-tipped, exceedingly sharp arrows, and it was scattered upon the ground.

sanskrit: chittvā tu śaktiṃ gāṅgeyaḥ sātyakiṃ navabhiḥ śaraiḥ ājaghānorasi kruddhaḥ prahasañ śatrukarśanaḥ
english: Having severed the lance, the son of Gaṅgā, wrathful yet laughing, that harrier of foes, struck Sātyaki in the chest with nine arrows.

sanskrit: tataḥ sarathanāgāśvāḥ pāṇḍavāḥ pāṇḍupūrvaja parivavrū raṇe bhīṣmaṃ mādhavatrāṇakāraṇāt
english: Then the Pāṇḍavas, O elder of the Pāṇḍu line, with their chariots, elephants, and horses, surrounded Bhīṣma in battle for the protection of the Mādhava.

sanskrit: tataḥ pravavṛte yuddhaṃ tumulaṃ lomaharṣaṇam pāṇḍavānāṃ kurūṇāṃ ca samare vijayaiṣiṇām
english: Then there broke out a tumultuous, hair-raising battle between the Pāṇḍavas and the Kurus, each longing for victory in the fray.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca dṛṣṭvā bhīṣmaṃ raṇe kruddhaṃ pāṇḍavair abhisaṃvṛtam yathā meghair mahārāja tapānte divi bhāskaram
english: Saṃjaya said: Seeing Bhīṣma wrathful in battle and hemmed in by the Pāṇḍavas, O great king, as the sun in the sky is wrapped by clouds at the end of the hot season—

sanskrit: duryodhano mahārāja duḥśāsanam abhāṣata eṣa śūro maheṣvāso bhīṣmaḥ śatruniṣūdanaḥ
english: Duryodhana, O great king, spoke to Duḥśāsana: "Here is the hero, the great archer Bhīṣma, slayer of foes,

sanskrit: chāditaḥ pāṇḍavaiḥ śūraiḥ samantād bharatarṣabha tasya kāryaṃ tvayā vīra rakṣaṇaṃ sumahātmanaḥ
english: covered on every side by the brave Pāṇḍavas, O bull of the Bhāratas. The protection of that exalted one must be your task, O hero.

sanskrit: rakṣyamāṇo hi samare bhīṣmo 'smākaṃ pitāmahaḥ nihanyāt samare yattān pāñcālān pāṇḍavaiḥ saha
english: For if guarded in battle, Bhīṣma our grandsire would slay the striving Pāñcālas together with the Pāṇḍavas.

sanskrit: tatra kāryam ahaṃ manye bhīṣmasyaivābhirakṣaṇam goptā hy eṣa maheṣvāso bhīṣmo 'smākaṃ pitāmahaḥ
english: Therein I deem the duty to be the safeguarding of Bhīṣma himself, for this great archer Bhīṣma, our grandsire, is our protector."

sanskrit: sa bhavān sarvasainyena parivārya pitāmaham samare duṣkaraṃ karma kurvāṇaṃ parirakṣatu
english: "Let you, then, with all the host, surround the grandsire and guard him as he works his hard deeds in battle."

sanskrit: evam uktas tu samare putro duḥśāsanas tava parivārya sthito bhīṣmaṃ sainyena mahatā vṛtaḥ
english: Thus addressed in the battle, your son Duḥśāsana took his stand encircling Bhīṣma, surrounded by a great host.

sanskrit: tataḥ śatasahasreṇa hayānāṃ subalātmajaḥ vimalaprāsahastānām ṛṣṭitomaradhāriṇām
english: Then the son of Subala, with a hundred thousand horsemen bearing gleaming javelins in hand, wielding spears and lances—

sanskrit: darpitānāṃ suvegānāṃ balasthānāṃ patākinām śikṣitair yuddhakuśalair upetānāṃ narottamaiḥ
english: proud, swift, mighty, and bannered, attended by trained men foremost among men, skilled in war—

sanskrit: nakulaṃ sahadevaṃ ca dharmarājaṃ ca pāṇḍavam nyavārayan naraśreṣṭhaṃ parivārya samantataḥ
english: held back Nakula and Sahadeva, and the Pāṇḍava Dharmarāja, foremost of men, surrounding them on every side.

sanskrit: tato duryodhano rājā śūrāṇāṃ hayasādinām ayutaṃ preṣayām āsa pāṇḍavānāṃ nivāraṇe
english: Then King Duryodhana sent ten thousand brave horsemen to hold back the Pāṇḍavas.

sanskrit: taiḥ praviṣṭair mahāvegair garutmadbhir ivāhave khurāhatā dharā rājaṃś cakampe ca nanāda ca
english: As they charged in, swift as Garuḍa in the battle, the earth, struck by their hooves, O king, both trembled and roared.

sanskrit: khuraśabdaś ca sumahān vājināṃ śuśruve tadā mahāvaṃśavanasyeva dahyamānasya parvate
english: And the mighty sound of the horses' hooves was then heard like that of a great bamboo forest burning upon a mountain.

sanskrit: utpatadbhiś ca tais tatra samuddhūtaṃ mahad rajaḥ divākarapathaṃ prāpya chādayām āsa bhāskaram
english: And the great dust raised up by their galloping there, reaching the path of the day-maker, veiled the sun.

sanskrit: vegavadbhir hayais tais tu kṣobhitaṃ pāṇḍavaṃ balam nipatadbhir mahāvegair haṃsair iva mahat saraḥ heṣatāṃ caiva śabdena na prājñāyata kiṃ cana
english: By those swift horses the Pāṇḍava force was thrown into turmoil, as a great lake is by geese descending at high speed; and amid the sound of their neighing nothing could be discerned.

sanskrit: tato yudhiṣṭhiro rājā mādrīputrau ca pāṇḍavau pratyaghnaṃs tarasā vegaṃ samare hayasādinām
english: Then King Yudhiṣṭhira and the two Pāṇḍava sons of Mādrī swiftly beat back the onrush of the horsemen in battle.

sanskrit: udvṛttasya mahārāja prāvṛṭkālena pūryataḥ paurṇamāsyām ambuvegaṃ yathā velā mahodadheḥ
english: As the shore checks the surging flood of the great ocean, swollen by the rainy season and risen at the full moon, O great king.

sanskrit: tatas te rathino rājañ śaraiḥ saṃnataparvabhiḥ nyakṛntann uttamāṅgāni kāyebhyo hayasādinām
english: Then those car-warriors, O king, with arrows of smoothly bent joints, severed the heads of the horsemen from their bodies.

sanskrit: te nipetur mahārāja nihatā dṛḍhadhanvibhiḥ nāgair iva mahānāgā yathā syur girigahvare
english: They fell, O great king, slain by those stout bowmen, like great elephants felled by elephants in a mountain cave.

sanskrit: te 'pi prāsaiḥ suniśitaiḥ śaraiḥ saṃnataparvabhiḥ nyakṛntann uttamāṅgāni vicaranto diśo daśa
english: They too, ranging through all ten directions, severed the heads of their foes with keen javelins and arrows of smoothly bent joints.

sanskrit: atyāsannā hayārohā ṛṣṭibhir bharatarṣabha acchinann uttamāṅgāni phalānīva mahādrumāt
english: Drawing very close, the horsemen with their spears cut off the heads of their foes, O bull of the Bhāratas, as one plucks fruits from a great tree.

sanskrit: sasādino hayā rājaṃs tatra tatra niṣūditāḥ patitāḥ pātyamānāś ca śataśo 'tha sahasraśaḥ
english: Horses with their riders, O king, were slain here and there—fallen and falling by the hundreds and the thousands.

sanskrit: vadhyamānā hayās te tu prādravanta bhayārditāḥ yathā siṃhān samāsādya mṛgāḥ prāṇaparāyaṇāḥ
english: Those horses, being slaughtered and stricken with terror, fled away, as deer that, meeting lions, flee bent on saving their lives.

sanskrit: pāṇḍavās tu mahārāja jitvā śatrūn mahāhave dadhmuḥ śaṅkhāṃś ca bherīś ca tāḍayām āsur āhave
english: And the Pāṇḍavas, O great king, having vanquished their foes in that great battle, blew their conches and beat their drums in the fray.

sanskrit: tato duryodhano dṛṣṭvā dīnaṃ sainyam avasthitam abravīd bharataśreṣṭha madrarājam idaṃ vacaḥ
english: Then Duryodhana, seeing his army standing crestfallen, O best of the Bhāratas, spoke these words to the king of the Madras:

sanskrit: eṣa pāṇḍusuto jyeṣṭho jitvā mātula māmakān paśyatāṃ no mahābāho senāṃ drāvayate balī
english: "This eldest son of Pāṇḍu, O maternal uncle, having conquered my men, even as we look on, O mighty-armed one, the strong one routs my army.

sanskrit: taṃ vāraya mahābāho veleva makarālayam tvaṃ hi saṃśrūyase 'tyartham asahyabalavikramaḥ
english: Hold him back, O mighty-armed one, as the shore holds back the abode of sea-monsters; for you are renowned beyond measure as one of unbearable strength and prowess."

sanskrit: putrasya tava tad vākyaṃ śrutvā śalyaḥ pratāpavān prayayau rathavaṃśena yatra rājā yudhiṣṭhiraḥ
english: Hearing that speech of your son, the majestic Śalya advanced with his line of chariots to where King Yudhiṣṭhira was.
